correctness.rationale: The Gram identity is exactly six moment cancellations plus unit mass. A six-node obstruction is proved by a generalized Vandermonde determinant factoring as the ordinary Vandermonde times the third elementary symmetric polynomial of six distinct eleventh roots; its twenty positive cyclotomic terms cannot sum to zero since 11 does not divide 20. For seven nodes, an ordinary Vandermonde transformation yields unique real candidate weights. The 20 exhaustive dihedral orbits and 160 Cramer determinant signs are checked using rational Machin/Taylor enclosures, 10^12-scaled entries, exact Bareiss determinants, strict 10^-3 determinant margins and a proved <10^-7 error bound. The saved CHECK.py was executed successfully. Quantifiers are restricted to Z_11 and E={0,1,2,3}.

value.rationale: The problem asks for the smallest strictly positive weighted exact Fourier sampling set on a fixed natural four-coordinate aperture and which minimizers actually work. Although abstract moment theory gives an implicit feasibility test and Carathéodory bounds, it does not supply the 33/330 selectivity or unexpected reflection rigidity. The complete 20-orbit, certified finite classification and arithmetic six-node impossibility distinguish genuine design possibilities, including unique optimal weights, at the first nontrivial eleven-point grid beyond the seven-point saturation case. This is a reusable exact benchmark for sparse harmonic-frame design; no downstream general theorem is asserted.
